items.title: Iconic winter sport is gaining popularity as a new experience in Mississauga
items.summary: With the sport only gaining more popularity in Ontario and throughout Canada, partly due to its place in the winter Olympics and its growing accessibility, curling is fast becoming a must-try activity. Mississauga’s Dixie Curling Centre, located at Applewood Heights Park, is known for being a fun hangout spot for people of all ages and skill levels, including those who have never curled before, in a spacious six-sheet facility. During each curling season the centre runs programs 14 hours a day, seven days a week, and there’s something for everyone here: Curling lessons for beginners, novice leagues, junior leagues, and advanced options including men’s, women’s and mixed leagues. With a long-standing tradition of being friendly and inclusive to all, Dixie Curling Centre is one of Ontario’s best places to try curling in a variety of different programs. Here’s a closer look at everything they offer: No matter what age or skill level, Dixie Curling Club is ready to teach you everything you’ll need to know about this beloved sport. Their adult Learn-to-Curl program is a five-week crash course led by friendly instructors, and all necessary equipment (slip-on grippers, step-on sliders, brooms, delivery sticks) is provided. By the end of this program, curlers have a good sense of delivery, sweeping, basic strategy, gameplay, etiquette, and proper curling form, giving them all the confidence they need to step out on the ice and ready to play a game. For little curlers as young as 7, the centre’s Little Rocks program offers a fun, affordable, and skill-building curling experience. Geared towards youth aged 7 to 20, this program features two hours of on-ice instruction and gameplay, tasty snacks, and opportunities to join bonspiels and competitive teams at the centre. The program is also budget-friendly, offering weekly two-hour sessions for 20 weeks for under $300.

items.title: Knights, horses and combat won’t be coming to Mississauga after fair cancelled
items.summary: A Renaissance Faire that was set to bring medieval combat, horses, birds of prey, vendors and other attractions to Mississauga later this month has been cancelled before it ever got off the ground. The Port Credit Renaissance Faire was scheduled for Aug. 29 and 30 at Port Credit Memorial Park, marking what organizers said would have been the first time the event was held in Mississauga. com and said logistical issues involving the City of Mississauga ultimately led to the decision to pull the plug. “I called Mississauga and told them I was pulling it,” the organizer said. She described the situation as a matter of difficulties working out the logistical and financial requirements for holding the event. Among the issues raised were requirements surrounding a mobile business licence for vendors. She said unanticipated additional costs were difficult to absorb given the other expenses involved in putting on the event, including park rental, insurance, fuel and advertising. The organizer said she had already invested in advertising and had attracted vendors who were interested in taking part.

items.title: Mississauga teen starts global organization helping students explore healthcare careers
items.summary: A Mississauga teen has started a global organization to help students explore careers in healthcare and medical research — and youth can learn more at a conference this weekend. The organization, Dr. Interested, now reaches 106 countries and has impacted over 160,000 people, said its founder and managing director, Adil Mukhi. Dr. Interested is holding a conference this weekend in Mississauga for youth to learn more about healthcare careers. Adil Mukhi is now 16 years old and will enter Grade 12 at Glenforest Secondary School’s International Baccalaureate program in Mississauga in the fall. Mukhi started Dr. Interested when he was 13 years old and in Grade 9. When he was in Grade 7 and 8, Adil felt career education was limited due to pandemic lockdowns. com. Adil explored future career paths on his own and found a few mentors. He worked with one mentor who helped him explore his future dream career in healthcare. “But I realized a lot of people didn’t have this, and so that’s what the organization came out of, as a way to help people learn about careers,” he said.

items.title: Rathwood's 20-Storey Rental Tower Would Gain a 144-Unit Neighbour Under New Proposal
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the City of Mississauga is reviewing an application to amend the official plan and zoning bylaw to allow a new 13-storey rental apartment building with 144 units at 1315 Bough Beeches Blvd. in the Rathwood neighbourhood, near Dixie and Rathburn roads. Mississauga.com reports the site already contains a 20-storey rental tower with 270 units, described in the applicant's planning report as a tower-in-the-park building surrounded by two surface parking lots, and that existing tower would remain in place under the proposal. The site's open space, including mature trees, a tennis court, a basketball court and a ramp to the underground parking garage, would also be preserved except for some of the surface parking. The application, prepared by WND Associates Ltd., notes the surrounding area includes one- and two-storey homes on Poltava Crescent to the north, Rathburn Road and the aging single-storey Rockwood Mall strip plaza to the south, a mid-rise apartment building and homes to the east, and a subdivision of townhouses and detached homes near Dixie Road to the west. Under the plan, the new building's residential units would occupy floors two through 13, while the ground floor would house the lobby, amenity spaces and loading and servicing areas.

items.title: Average Home in Mississauga Now Sells for Under $900,000 as Prices Keep Sliding
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, citing new data from the Toronto Regional Real Estate Board, the average home price in Mississauga fell 11.4 per cent year-over-year to $899,002 in July 2026. Mississauga.com reports the city recorded 500 home sales in July, with homes spending an average of 32 days on the market before selling, while 2,518 listings remained active by the end of the month. The board's breakdown showed 184 detached houses sold during the month, averaging 28 days on the market with 945 active listings, alongside 69 semi-detached sales averaging 26 days on the market and 204 active listings, and 23 attached house sales averaging 31 days on the market with 62 active listings. Townhouse-style condos saw their average price slide to $712,285, down roughly 2 per cent both month-over-month and year-over-year, on 95 sales that averaged 31 days on the market with 406 active listings by month's end. Mississauga.com reports the figures point to a broader cooling across most segments of the city's housing market in July.

items.title: Former Raptors head coach Nick Nurse says Ontario owes him nearly $700,000 — and he’s fighting for it
items.summary: Nurse and his wife are appealing the foreign buyer’s tax they paid on their Mississauga home after being told they didn’t meet residency requirements. Nurse was fired from the Raptors in 2023 and was hired shortly afterward by the Philadelphia 76ers. Nick Nurse reacts to a call while he was head coach of the Raptors in a game against the Utah Jazz in February, 2023. Nurse is appealing to have $697,500 in taxes he paid on his former Mississauga home returned to him by the Ontario government. 65 million Mississauga home. The couple are arguing they legally qualified for a rebate of the Non-Resident Speculation Tax, a levy designed to discourage foreign speculation in Ontario’s housing market. According to their notice of appeal, they were denied because, they say, they were told by the Ministry of Finance that they failed to meet residency requirements. Nurse and his wife Roberta “are simply following the appeal process set out in the Land Transfer Tax Act to challenge a statement of disallowance that, in our view, is incorrect,” the couple’s lawyer, Mike Collinge, told the Star Tuesday. The Ministry of Finance did not respond to the Star’s questions. Nurse, an Iowa native, joined the Toronto Raptors in 2013 and coached the team to its first National Basketball Association championship in 2019. He was fired in April 2023 after a disappointing season in which the Raptors failed to make the playoffs. Less than two months later, he was hired as head coach of the Philadelphia 76ers.
